data: Before we head out, how about we agree to catch 10 tons each this month? That leaves 50 tons to double back to 100, so we can each earn $10,000 a month without running down the lake. My family has fished here for years, and I want our village to keep making a living from it. Let’s check the reported catches together each month and agree on the next month’s limits before fishing. John, would you be willing to stick to 10 tons?

I’m in for 10 tons, Luke. My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season, and this gives all five of us a steady living. If the lake ever starts a month below 100 tons, let’s agree on lower whole-ton limits so it can recover. John, can you commit to 10 this month too?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want the village’s children to have the same chance. Let’s make 50 tons our combined ceiling, not a target to exceed if someone takes less, and review the reported catches together each month. Kate, are you willing to join us at 10?

I’ll stick to 10 tons. A reliable living for all our families matters more than one big haul. If someone goes over the limit, let’s discuss it and adjust next month’s catches to help the lake recover—not race to empty it. John, will you join us at 10?

I’m in—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. My family taught me that leaving fish in the lake protects our next catch and our neighbors’ livelihoods. That’s all five of us agreed: 10 tons each, then we’ll review the reported catches together before next month.

Thanks, everyone—we have an agreement. I’ll catch 10 tons this month. Let’s meet here again after the catches are reported to check the lake’s stock and plan next month. Here’s to a steady living for all five families.
